title: Appearance is below the fold again, because the panel still wants more room than the window has
goal: With a piece of text picked in a three layer document, the right hand panel asks for more height than the tallest window this display can give it, and the section that lost the argument is Appearance: its last stretch now sits below the bottom of the panel where it used to be on screen. You asked on 2026-09-07 that Appearance and Effects are the two sections nobody should ever have to scroll to, and shipped work has quietly walked that back. Decide how the panel keeps that promise when what it wants does not fit, and make it keep it.
notes:
From the 2026-09-16 design review, and the evidence is two rough lines the panel-sections task wrote about its own work (queue/audits/2026-09-15-panel-sections.json):

  "The panel is still over-subscribed by a factor, not by a few points. With a piece of text picked in a three layer document it wants 1052 points and the tallest window this display gives it is 968. Nothing was made shorter; the change only decides which sections are allowed to ask."
  "Appearance pays for it. At 1200 by 720 with text picked it now runs 497 to 720 in a 688 point panel, so its last 32 points are below the fold where they used to be on screen. With an arrow picked it is 382 points tall and lands at 681 in a 688 point panel."
  "This partly walks back what the user asked for on 2026-09-07, that Appearance and Effects are the two sections that must never need scrolling to. It is a real trade and the evaluate list above asks about it directly rather than hiding it."

Why this is filed as its own task rather than folded: the panel's height has now been attacked seven separate times with local fixes, every one of them done (the-panel-stops-explaining-itself-in-paragraphs, picking-a-text-layer-leaves-its-settings-below-t, position-and-size-leave-the-panel, one-row-for-a-number-that-has-four-sides, the-panel-shows-the-panes-that-matter, position-and-size-stays-on-screen-when-you-pick, the-h-field-in-the-text-section-can-be-out-of-re), and the panel still asks for 1052 in a 968. Each of those bought back points. None of them changed the fact that the sections together want more than any window has, which is why the next feature that wants room takes it from Appearance again.

Related and NOT the same thing: photograph-the-sections-row-and-measure-what-it (nobody has seen the Sections row drawn or measured what turning a section off really buys) and the-motion-section-sits-directly-under-effects-w (Motion is eleven sections below Effects). Do those two first if all three are open: this one needs their numbers.
acceptance: With a piece of text picked, Appearance is fully on screen without scrolling, at the window sizes a person actually uses
The same is true of Effects
The rule is written down where the next section to be added will be read against it, so this does not get walked back again by the next feature that wants room
The panel's asked-for height and the height it is given are both measured and reported, before and after, at a window size named in the audit
It is checked with an arrow picked as well as with text, because those two ask for different sections

Section 3 of docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md gains the rule this answer settles: which sections a panel column may push below the fold, what it owes the one it pushes, and what a new section has to prove before it may join the column, citing this task and the 2026-09-16 and 2026-09-17 crowding cases

log.note: created (manual)
claimed by go loop

MEASURED, before any change. The Mac's screen was locked for this whole turn, so no walk could run (every one exits 3 with status locked) and no picture was possible. Instead I read back the 3,334 recorded panel states that 185 walks left in /tmp/photonz-playtest earlier today. At a 1200x720 window the dock is 621pt, 609 shareable; Appearance or Effects was below the fold in 44% of states there, 50% at 781pt, and 12% even at the 969pt dock of the largest window this display opens. Worked cases at 1200x720: text 163+198+231+68=747 (over 126); arrow 163+447+68=765 (over 144); component copy 163+311+195+68=1102 (over 481); measurement 163+109+489+68=702 (over 81).

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, before building: the mock-equivalent here is the seven previous fixes, and they are wrong. All seven were ORDERING changes, and ordering only decides WHICH section is left below the fold, never how many points there are. The thing none of them knew is in the numbers above: Appearance is not a small form, it is the BIGGEST section in the dock. It is a list of the parts a thing is made of and every switched-on part unfolds all of its settings at once (PartsInspector -> ShapePartSettings), so an arrow is 447pt of it and a measurement 489pt. The tallest Appearance recorded all day is 669pt, which is MORE THAN THE WHOLE 621pt DOCK. DockMetrics.scrollingSections still classifies Appearance as a form, so it is the only one of the promised sections the height budget may never shorten. An eighth ordering fix would have walked something else back; I did not write one.

SHIPPED, mechanism-independent: acceptance item 3 (the rule written down where the next section is read against it). Sources/Photonz/InspectorDockLayout.swift now carries a third rule beside the two it already had about order and cast: a rule about HEIGHT, with the budget arithmetic, the four worked cases, the percentages and the two findings. It says a section may not be added, and an existing one may not grow, without naming which line of that table it spends from. That file is what every panel change reads first. swift build clean; Scripts/test.sh green, 7662 tests in 615 suites.

BLOCKED on a decision rather than guessing an eighth time. The three ways out are visibly different products and the arithmetic says no single one covers every case: (a) let the budget shorten Appearance, so the fold is guaranteed by construction and Appearance scrolls inside itself when it must - the only answer that cannot fail; (b) Appearance folds one part at a time like the Effects list, which fixes arrow and measurement but leaves text over by 15pt and a component copy by 93pt; (c) the layers list moves to a left dock, which hands back 163pt and fixes three of four but not a measurement. Recommended (a). Card and brief filed. Acceptance items 1, 2, 4-after and 5 are unverifiable this turn anyway: they all need a walk, and a walk needs an unlocked screen.

left rough, not filed: Appearance is declared a form in DockMetrics.scrollingSections while being a variable-length list of parts. That misclassification is the mechanical cause of everything above, but fixing it IS option (a), so it belongs to this task's decision and not to a task of its own. No audit written: nothing shipped that a person can try, so an audit would have had nothing to put in its try list and no picture to put beside it.

Measured and written down; the fix needs an answer. At 1200x720 the dock has 609pt and is asked for 660-1102, so Appearance or Effects is below the fold 44% of the time, and Appearance alone reaches 669pt - taller than the whole panel. Seven previous fixes were all re-orderings, which only move which section loses. The three real ways out are visibly different products and none covers every case alone, so a decision card is open (recommended: let the height budget shorten Appearance, the only answer that cannot fail). The measurement and the budget rule shipped in InspectorDockLayout.swift regardless of the answer; b90b6e7b.

Design review 2026-09-17: this is the one IA finding of the cycle and it is getting worse rather than waiting quietly. Two more sections landed in the same column in the last 24 hours (Motion moved under Effects, queue/audits/2026-09-16-motion-under-effects.json; the Sections row shipped and was then corrected twice for counting wrong). The card has been up since 2026-09-16 16:46Z. A scrub item has been added to two-rules-in-ux-patterns-get-scrubbed-a-callout so that whichever way you answer, the rule is written down and the next section does not have to work it out again.

Folded in from the UX-PATTERNS scrub (two-rules-in-ux-patterns-get-scrubbed-a-callout, 2026-09-17). The shared patterns document has no rule for what a panel column owes when its sections want more height than the window can give: which sections it may push below the fold, what it owes the one it pushes, and what a new section has to prove before it may join the column. Section 3's height rule stops at 'when it still does not fit, the dock scrolls and nothing is thrown away', which says what must not happen and not who loses. The answer to the card on this task settles it, so the rule is written by whoever does this task, not before. Cases to cite when writing it: this task, the Sections row added on 2026-09-17 partly to manage the same crowding, and Motion moving under Effects (queue/audits/2026-09-16-motion-under-effects.json), which is one more section in the same column.

More evidence from separate-into-layers work on 2026-09-18, and it adds a case the other seven fixes did not cover: after Separate into Layers on Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/Fixtures/settings-pane-2x.png the document holds 24 layers, and the Layers list shows FIVE rows. Reaching the two cards at the bottom of the tree takes two scrolls in a playtest (Scripts/playtest/separate-boxes-walk.json now does exactly that). The twist: in that same window the sections under it are EMPTY - Effects says 'Nothing yet. Add one with the plus above.' and Motion says 'Nothing moves yet.' - and roughly the bottom third of the dock is blank. So this is not only over-subscription; a section with nothing in it is still holding height the list could have had. Picture: queue/audits/2026-09-18-separate-2-layers-list.png.

Design review 2026-09-18, folded in with an ACCEPTANCE ADDITION (there is no queue.mjs command to edit acceptance, so treat this line as one): a section the panel has squeezed must say it has been squeezed, and today only one of them does. queue/audits/2026-09-17-shelf-stays-put.json: 'The Library is the only self-bounding section in the panel that fades its cut edge. The layers list bounds itself the same way and still ends on a clean cut, so a squeezed layers list reads as the whole document.' queue/audits/2026-09-18-separate-into-layers.json then shows the cost of that in the focus feature: after Separate into Layers the document holds 24 layers and the list shows FIVE rows, on a clean cut, so the list reads as the whole document when it is a fifth of it. So the rule this task writes into UX-PATTERNS section 3 has to answer 'what it owes the one it pushes' for a section cut short as well as for one pushed below the fold, and whatever it settles has to apply to the layers list, not only to the Library shelf.

The video design pass (2026-09-19) measured what a document with TIME does to this. The bottom dock is a full width band under the canvas AND the panel, so the panel loses its whole height: 88 points for a recording just opened, 235 at its ceiling, which takes a 968 point dock down to 733. The same selection that fits today at 962 of 968 is then 189 points over, and on a laptop window (688 minus 235 = 453) it is over 280 points over. Arithmetic in Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/DockWithTimeTests.swift, eight tests, and in docs/design/video-surface.md section 4. So whatever answers this task has to survive a panel 200 points shorter than the one it is being designed against.
decision "Appearance and Effects will not both fit a laptop window. How should the panel keep them on screen?" resolved: Guarantee the fold

Measured again on 2026-09-20 from position-and-size-on-screen-walk, with numbers: a three layer document with a piece of text picked asks the dock for 1052 points, and the largest window this display gives hands it 941, so the last 30 points of Effects sit under the fold. 1052 is exactly what the panel asked before the four Position & Size boxes were taken out of it on 2026-09-15, so the 130 points that change gave back have all been taken again by what arrived after: the sections now read Layers 6-169, Text 169-367, Appearance 367-599, Effects 599-971, Motion 971-1052. The walk used to claim Effects was whole at that size and now claims only that its header is in view, with the reason written into the step, so this is not being quietly dropped.

another section joined the panel on 2026-09-21: Sound, for a layer that plays one (next-sound-on-the-timeline). It sits directly above Motion, which in a normal window puts the Level fader at the very bottom of the dock - and Level is the most reached control a sound layer has. Same shape of problem this task is about, one more section deep.

also happens to Sound: the 2026-09-21-video-audio audit says the Sound section sits at the bottom of the panel, under Motion, and the level fader is the most reached control a sound layer has and the lowest thing in the dock. Same shape as Appearance: whatever shipped last lands lowest, whatever it is used for. Whatever fixes the ordering has to be a rule about what a layer is being used for, not a hand-ordered list, or the next feature repeats it.

Another section pushed below the fold by the same crowding, on 2026-09-21: the new Speed section (next-speed-a-stretch) sits under Layers, Appearance, Effects, Reframe, Motion and Transition, so on a video document you scroll past six sections to reach the one property of the clip you are most likely to be changing. Seen in queue/audits/2026-09-21-video-speed.json and in speed-2-the-same-take-at-four-times-sc.png, where the speed list is cut off at the bottom edge of the panel.

Another one, from hold-on-a-frame (2026-09-21): with a clip picked in a video document the Time section (holding a frame, and the speeds) is below Reframe, Motion and Transition, so freezing the frame you are looking at costs a scroll before the first click. The video sections arrive in a run at the bottom and they are the ones a person is using while they watch.

Also true with a TITLE picked on a video document (2026-09-21, a-title-is-text-that-knows-when-it-is-on-screen): the Time section holds when the words arrive and leave and the Fade choices, and it sits under Text, Appearance, Effects and Motion, so the Fade list is below the fold in a 1080 window. Picture: queue/audits/2026-09-21-title-4-fades-on-sc.png.

Another section fell below the fold on 2026-09-21: with a component picked on a recording, the Time section (when it arrives, when it goes, Start Here, End Here, Fade) is the LAST section before Library, under Component, Appearance, Effects, Motion and Layout. On a document with a timeline that is the one question the panel is being asked, and it is the furthest thing down. Seen in queue/audits/2026-09-22-components-on-the-timeline-1.png.
